title: FOOTSTOOL & AN OLD GLADSTONE B...
findings: Two photos. Beside it an old Gladstone (doctor's style) bag in reptile-grain leather with a leather-covered steel frame, plain steel knobs, one leather carry handle and an end strap with buckle. condition: Bag: very dry and cracked leather with heavy loss of finish, dark staining and scuffed corners, frame leather lifting, hardware rusty; interior not shown. Stool: velvet worn and faded, pine clean with minor marks; lid hinge and interior not shown.

title: SET OF 6 COPELAND SPODE ENTREE...
description: SET OF 6 COPELAND SPODE ENTREE PLATES
findings: Six matching plates, each decorated with a large blue leaf with white dotted edge and red veins, pink and orange flowers, a blue branch border and a red-brown rim. Photo 2 shows the base of one plate with a printed blue cartouche mark reading 'COPELAND late SPODE ENGLAND' (the word ENGLAND puts it after 1891, and this Copeland late Spode mark ran well into the 20th century) plus a hand-painted red pattern number that is rotated and soft but reads as '2/6207', with a small extra red mark beside it (possibly a painter's or gilder's mark). Spode pattern 2/6207 is listed in Spode references as the 'Cabbage' pattern (a Tobacco Leaf style design) reissued on earthenware in 1910 to 1911, which matches the blue leaf with red and pink colouring seen. So the title's Copeland Spode is supported, while the pattern name and approximate date (about 1910s) are not in the title. Only one base was photographed, so the other five bases are unchecked, but all six fronts show the same pattern. Plate diameter is not stated and cannot be measured from the photos.
condition: No chips, cracks or rim damage visible on the fronts. Two plates show brownish staining or discolouration in the well (top left and bottom left), which may be tea staining with crazing. Some rubbing to the red edge line. Bases other than one not seen.
reason: Set of six Copeland late Spode plates in the collectable blue leaf 'Cabbage' pattern (number reads 2/6207, about 1910s), which the title does not name.
marks_read: Printed blue 'COPELAND late SPODE ENGLAND' mark; hand-painted red pattern no. reads 2/6207 (rotated, soft)

title: DIOR MAMME MEDIUM MENS DOUBLE ...
description: DIOR MAMME MEDIUM MENS DOUBLE BREASTED TRENCH COAT
findings: Five photos of a black wool-blend double-breasted military-style belted long coat with epaulettes, two rows of silver-tone crest buttons (crown and wreath crest, no lettering), buckled cuff tabs, red piping on the inner front facing, black quilted satin diamond lining and a back belt. The only label is a black woven rectangle at the back neck with white dashed contrast stitching reading, in white script, 'Dior Homme' with 'size M' in small slab-serif type beneath (photo 3 close-up; the title's 'DIOR MAMME' is a misreading of the script). This does not match genuine Dior Homme labelling as far as I can tell: genuine pieces carry plain woven 'Dior' or 'Dior Homme' neck labels, a separate Paris loop tag, a care and composition label and European numeric sizes, and the buttons would normally carry Dior marking. No composition, care, made-in or Paris tag is visible. The Dior attribution is therefore not supported and the coat looks like a lookalike or replica of a military coat.
condition: Black wool shows dust, lint and surface specks over the back and shoulders with some light pilling; loose thread at the belt end; lining intact as far as seen; no holes noted. Size M per the label.
reason: Script 'Dior Homme size M' label, crest buttons and no care or Paris tag do not look genuine; likely a lookalike coat of modest value.
marks_read: Script label 'Dior Homme' and 'size M' (non-standard, doubtful); buttons crown and wreath crest, no lettering
